passage.title: Text One, 'The Last Ferry' (teacher-written modern travel memoir for TGA)
paras: The harbour smelled of diesel and wet rope. The ferry was forty minutes late, and the six of us waiting on the slipway had stopped pretending to read. A gull stood on a bollard and stared at us as though we owed it money.

When we finally cast off, the sea was the colour of wet slate, and it moved like something breathing in its sleep. Each wave lifted the bow, held it, and let it drop, as if the sea were weighing us and could not decide. Nobody spoke. The engine spoke for all of us.

Halfway across, the light went. The mainland behind us shrank to a smudge; ahead there was nothing at all. I gripped the rail and thought, absurdly, of my own kitchen: the kettle, the clock, the ordinary safety I had been so keen to escape.

Then, quite suddenly, the island was there: a low grey line, then a single lamp, then a door opening. Someone on the quay was holding out a hand. I have travelled a long way since, but I have never been so grateful to arrive anywhere.

questions.q: Read Text One (pupil PDF). Give one thing the writer compares the sea to in paragraph 2 .
questions.a: Something breathing in its sleep (or: the colour of wet slate).
questions.model: Underline the focus (paragraph 2, compares). Scan only that paragraph. Write the detail, nothing more: 'Something breathing in its sleep.'

questions.q: Give two things the writer thinks about when the light goes .
questions.a: Any two: her kitchen; the kettle; the clock; the ordinary safety she wanted to escape.

questions.q: Core: complete the error analysis sheet for your baseline paper, then write two targets in the portal response box. Starter: 'In Section ___ I lost marks because... Next time I will...'

questions.q: Explain the effect of 'the ordinary safety I had been so keen to escape' (paragraph 3).
questions.a: Irony: the writer now longs for the safety she once found boring, which shows how frightened she is.
questions.model: Method: contrast and irony. Evidence: 'ordinary safety' against 'keen to escape'. Effect: the dull home she fled now seems precious; fear has changed her values.
